items.finding: The multi-label generality of the shared pattern ('(?:[A-Z0-9]+ )*', which v1.0.8 describes as covering any PEM private-key header label) is not pinned by any test: narrowing it to at most one label (reviewer mutant X05) survives the author's suites and the reviewer's probes. No standard multi-word private-key label is known to be affected.

Framings outside five-dash PEM armor (the SSH2 four-dash 'BEGIN SSH2 ENCRYPTED PRIVATE KEY' form, the PuTTY key-file form) are detected by neither scanner, before or after this delta. At link.repo the grammar excludes them; elsewhere in a projection they STOP only if another detector (typically OPAQUE_HIGH_ENTROPY on the body) fires.

The documented grammar is a repository-CREATION rule, not a stated contract on the name field of GET /user/repos or on Vercel's link.repo, and it does not encode reserved names. A real name outside it would STOP (availability, not safety).

The EC-1 re-scan grammar layer is the ONLY grammar guard in the standalone EC-1 CLI (isAdjudicatedValue = () => true): without it a forged marker explains a grammar-invalid entropy value. Present in the candidate; the standalone-CLI weakness itself is the earlier record's NB-4, still OPEN.

Successor-chain contiguity is still not code-enforced: a successor candidate arms with the fixed b25f2d32 event and its own event, whether or not this 00d6d383 event has been added to the fixed list. The successor duty remains procedural (the earlier record's NB-5).

Wording: v1.0.8 says a private-key header 'anywhere in a projection' STOPs; G-R5 pages are by design reduced to target matches before the scan, so a non-matching repository's name on a G-R5 page is discarded unscanned (never recorded).

The executor's detector layer and the grammar layer overlap exactly for private keys (every PEM header contains a space): reviewer mutant X15 (private key made deferrable, grammar kept) is EQUIVALENT and survives. Each layer is independently sufficient (measured in both directions), but only layer-combination removal can show it.
